methods.name: Complete nonzero equality classification for two-positive raw X6 stability
triggers: two positive raw X6 equality rectangle classification

methods.input_contract: Finite positive rational populations in one common external anchor and labelled signed X6 frame. First aggregate and Jordan-cancel; require p(f)<=2 and M=||f||_1>0. D is the sum of all twenty complete raw three-axis L1 norms. Negative support and coordinate spans are initially arbitrary and finite; equal total mass is not assumed.
methods.output_contract: D=4M if and only if the original raw signed difference is an equal-weight coordinate rectangle: two positive diagonal corners and two negative off-diagonal corners, every absolute mass w>0. Exactly two axes vary between arbitrary distinct integer endpoints; the other four axes agree. Equality forces equal total masses. An arbitrary common positive population may be added before cancellation.
methods.core_law: The complete nonnegative gap D-4M equals the sum of tablewise L1 dual gaps and negative-support penalties. Equality forces original negative support onto the two crossed rectangle corners; zero L-table signed rows then force all four weights equal. This argument classifies original coordinates without inverting an irreversible compression.
methods.hard_boundary: Zero M=D=0 is excluded. The result does not classify p>=3 equality, require unit edge lengths, or authorize arbitrary rotation, shear or can3-only equivalence. It does not recover microscopic BRC or branch history. The old paper's then-unclassified historical statement is left unchanged; this later paper supplies the precise extension, with no formal acceptance or executable API.

methods.name: Three-positive raw X6 unequal-mass witness and a specified symmetric equal-mass family
triggers: three positive raw X6 unequal mass boundary 7/26

methods.input_contract: Same-anchor labelled signed X6 positive rational populations, aggregated and Jordan-cancelled before p is counted. The specific family has positive unit masses at 100,010,001 and negative masses a at 000, b at each of 110,101,011, and c at 111, with a,b,c>=0 and the other three axes fixed. Zero negative weights are omitted. D is the sum of all twenty raw three-axis L1 norms.
methods.output_contract: The seven-point member a=b=1,c=0 has p=3,P=3,N=4,M=7,D=26, so the arbitrary-mass optimal constant is at least 7/26>1/4. For the specified symmetric family N=a+3b+c and M=3+N, the paper gives the exact piecewise formula for D. In this family's equal-mass slice N=3, D>=4M and equality holds exactly when c=0, 1/2<=b<=2/3, a=3-3b; then M=6,D=24.
methods.core_law: Group the twenty raw tables by their number of active axes: multiplicities 1,9,9,1. The exact positive/negative address ledgers give D=M+|3-N|+9(|2-a-b|+|1-2b-c|)+9(|1-a|+2|1-b|+b+c). On N=3 the gap is D-24=18c+36(1-2b-c)_++18(3b+c-2)_+.
methods.hard_boundary: 7/26 is a demonstrated lower bound, not a sharp or global upper bound. The seven-point witness has unequal total masses and is not an equal-mass counterexample. D>=4M and the stated equality interval apply only to the specified symmetric family; they do not bound all equal-mass p=3 inputs. No arbitrary-mass family optimization, general p>=3 upper bound, consumer execution, microscopic BRC recovery or formal promotion is claimed.
